english: Three normals are drawn from a point $N(h,k)$ to the parabola $y^{2}=6x$, and their feet are the points $P$, $Q$ and $R$. The tangents to the parabola at $P$ and $Q$ meet at the point $T\left(-6,\dfrac{3}{2}\right)$. Then the value of $h$ is ______.
hindi: एक बिन्दु $N(h,k)$ से परवलय $y^{2}=6x$ पर तीन अभिलम्ब खींचे जाते हैं, जिनके पाद बिन्दु $P$, $Q$ तथा $R$ हैं। $P$ तथा $Q$ पर परवलय की स्पर्श रेखाएँ बिन्दु $T\left(-6,\dfrac{3}{2}\right)$ पर मिलती हैं। तब $h$ का मान ______ है।
solution_full: For $y^{2}=6x$, $4a=6$, $a=\dfrac{3}{2}$. Let the feet be $P,Q,R$ with parameters $t_{1},t_{2},t_{3}$, i.e. points $\left(\dfrac{3}{2}t^{2},3t\right)$.

The tangents at $t_{1}$ and $t_{2}$ are $t_{1}y=x+at_{1}^{2}$ and $t_{2}y=x+at_{2}^{2}$; they meet at $(at_{1}t_{2},\,a(t_{1}+t_{2}))$. Equating with $T\left(-6,\dfrac{3}{2}\right)$: $\dfrac{3}{2}t_{1}t_{2}=-6$ and $\dfrac{3}{2}(t_{1}+t_{2})=\dfrac{3}{2}$, so $t_{1}t_{2}=-4$, $t_{1}+t_{2}=1$. ($t_{1},t_{2}$ are the roots of $t^{2}-t-4=0$, real and distinct.)
The normal at $t$ is $y=-tx+2at+at^{3}$. It passes through $N(h,k)$ when $at^{3}+(2a-h)t-k=0$. This cubic has the roots $t_{1},t_{2},t_{3}$ (the three co-normal feet), and it has no $t^{2}$ term.
Also $t_{1}t_{2}t_{3}=\dfrac{k}{a}$ gives $k=\dfrac{3}{2}\cdot4=6$. Check with the normal at $t_{3}=-1$: $y=x-3-\dfrac{3}{2}=x-\dfrac{9}{2}$, and at $x=\dfrac{21}{2}$, $y=6$.
originality_note: New: the meeting point of the tangents at two co-normal feet is given, and the common point of the normals is recovered from it through Vieta's relations (way 5; the link is that T fixes t1 t2 and t1 + t2, and the zero sum then fixes the third foot). Closest known: 'tangents at the feet of three co-normals form a triangle; its centroid / orthocentre' and 'normals from (h,k): sum of parameters zero'. Different because: the problem runs backwards from one tangent intersection to N, needing both the tangent-intersection formula and the co-normal cubic.

concept_use.Normals to Parabola: Maximum of 3 co-nor: The co-normal cubic at^3 + (2a - h)t - k = 0 gives t1 + t2 + t3 = 0 and the sum of pairwise products (2a - h)/a, which yields h.
concept_use.Point of intersection of two tangents /: The tangents at P and Q meet at (a t1 t2, a(t1 + t2)); matching this with T gives t1 t2 = -4 and t1 + t2 = 1.

stem_review: Read as a student: every curve and point is defined before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed with sympy and checked by an independent numerical route, is unique and matches the Answer Plan; no hyperbolic functions or asymptotes. Checked that the feet P, Q are real and distinct (t^2 - t - 4 = 0), that R (t = -1) differs from both, that the three normals concur at N(21/2, 6) (sympy), and that 10.50 is a positive decimal as planned. Changed: the first design (area of the triangle formed by the tangents at the three feet) was replaced because the same tangent-triangle configuration appears in published questions.
key_step: Reading t1 t2 and t1 + t2 from T, then using the zero sum and the pairwise-product relation of the co-normal cubic.
justification: Two standard ideas linked in reverse (tangent intersection and co-normal Vieta relations), numerical answer, no heavy computation. Average Advanced, like the parabola tangent/normal chain 2024-P2-Q7 (L2) plus one more genuine link.
